USMLE-style practice · Orthopedics

Proximal fragment viability

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 29-year-old woman sustains a fracture through the scaphoid waist after a fall onto an extended wrist. At follow-up, the surgeon explains why the proximal fragment requires careful monitoring for impaired viability. Which anatomic feature best explains this concern?

  1. The scaphoid is supplied only by the ulnar nerve
  2. Much of the proximal scaphoid blood supply travels from distal entry points
  3. The scaphoid has no blood supply before injury
  4. All blood enters the proximal pole and flows distally
  5. The proximal fragment is supplied exclusively by synovial fluid
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Much of the proximal scaphoid blood supply travels from distal entry points

A fracture can interrupt the blood supply reaching the proximal fragment.

Understanding the options

Much of the proximal scaphoid blood supply travels from distal entry points
A fracture can interrupt the blood supply reaching the proximal fragment.
The scaphoid has no blood supply before injury
It has a blood supply, but the distribution makes some fragments vulnerable.
All blood enters the proximal pole and flows distally
This reverses the clinically important pattern.
The proximal fragment is supplied exclusively by synovial fluid
Synovial fluid is not the primary blood supply to the bone.
The scaphoid is supplied only by the ulnar nerve
Nerves do not provide the arterial perfusion described.
